That was the first room that I toured, and this was the room in front of which there was a double set of guards.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: I asked you about all rooms. After this room, where did you go next?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After that I remember going to a hangar. This is where they took me. I didn't know the premises. I didn't know where prisoners of war were held. In this hangar, there was a large number of POWs. They had candles that they put on some chairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: All right. You described that to us. What was the next room?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The next room was one containing fewer number of prisoners of war, 30 to 40.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: How many rooms there were in total containing prisoners of war?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know because I only saw three rooms. Prisoners of war were in the rooms to which the members of the military police took them.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: When you assigned tasks about the evacuation and boarding, I suppose that you had to tell each officer which room he had to evacuate?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't know exactly how many rooms there were. I didn't know how many prisoners of war there were. All I know was how many officers there were. I also knew that the military police was securing each room with prisoners of war. Since I acted in the way I described to you and assigned tasks to specific officers, if there had been any other prisoners of war, Borisavljevic would have told me, Sekic would have told me, that we needed more buses to evacuate these people.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: When you entered the Velepromet facility, did you see whether there was anybody standing outside in the yard?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the yard there was several women. I remember that there was a woman with a child. I also remember a lady who -- whom I remembered quite well. She held a big bag in her hands. I asked her whether she had a husband there. She said: Yes. Later on she was in the KP Dom camp, and I think this other woman with a child was also there in this correctional penitentiary facility camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: In addition to these women, there was no one else in the yard? Everyone else was locked inside these rooms?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Did these women remain in the yard when you started the evacuation?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They were there just during those 10 to 15 minutes while we were trying to assess the situation, either visually or by putting questions. All other women were already on the buses travelling in the column from Velepromet to Negoslavci.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, where were you when you heard that the buses had arrived?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you that -- I can't remember that moment clearly now, but they informed me. Perhaps it was while I was touring the facility that they informed me that the buses had arrived, meaning that they had arrived in front of Velepromet or were somewhere in the vicinity.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Who accompanied these buses?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Did they have any kind of escort, the buses?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had to have.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: If you were the one issuing an order to evacuate people, if you boarded people on buses, I suppose you had to ascertain who was going to escort these buses?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only within the compound. Outside of the compound was outside of my scope of authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Does this mean that you were authorised to send them out unescorted?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: That's why I'm asking you whether you came to meet the unit which was supposed to provide security to the buses while they travelled.

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Would you please wait for me to finish my question. Did you come to meet the unit which was supposed to provide security to the prisoners you had evacuated?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. If that had been my duty, then Major Sljivancanin would have brought that officer and introduced him to me. At least that's how it should have been in my view, had that been my task, but that wasn't my task.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Did you see any military police members that arrived there?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, except for the officer who was commander of the armoured combat vehicle that I used in order to establish military law and order within the Velepromet compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: The buses that you ordered should enter the compound of Velepromet, were there any military policemen on them?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see that either.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: So you sent the buses outside of the Velepromet compound without ascertaining whether they had any security?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That's not what I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: What did you do then?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The buses were taken over by the commander of the military police company which created the necessary conditions for evacuation to Mitrovica. As is well known, this person is now chief of the General Staff of the Macedonian army. At the time, he was a member of the battalion of the military police under the command of Colonel Mrksic -- or perhaps he wasn't. Perhaps he wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Are you saying that Colonel Mrksic had military police battalion under his command?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Colonel Mrksic did have a military police battalion, or perhaps even two.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you about the unit which was supposed to take over.

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know to whom this unit belonged. I don't know to whom the buses belonged, to which unit, to which logistics base.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Isn't it a typical procedure for somebody conducting an evacuation and handing over people to another unit which is supposed to secure them to go and meet the commander of that unit and to ascertain that all the necessary conditions are there?

utterances.speaker: BOGDAN VUJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When Major Sljivancanin sent me out to accomplish this mission, he didn't take me to Velepromet himself. I arrived there in the way that I described to you. Had this been his duty, he should have taken me to this facility. Captain Borisavljevic was duty-bound to handover the buses to the relevant commander in charge of the military police unit providing security to the buses which were travelling to Sremska Mitrovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think that we have used up all of our time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Vasic. We will adjourn now until tomorrow at 2.15. If counsel can be very conscious of the time issue that the Chamber has mentioned in preparing their cross-examination and in the course of tomorrow. We will adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 21st day of February, 2006, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.00 p.m.,
